title: 7.2 Energy Fluctuation in Canonical Ensemble
description: Although the canonical ensemble technically allows energy fluctuations, these fluctuations are negligible for macroscopic thermodynamic systems. As a result, the vast majority of systems in the ensemble reside within an extremely narrow energy range centered at the value determined by the temperature $T$. Hence, the canonical ensemble becomes equivalent to the microcanonical ensemble.

title: 7.6 Equivalence of canonical Ensemble and Grand Canonical Ensemble
description: If $\partial P/\partial v < 0$, nearly all systems in the grand canonical ensemble have the same particle number $N$ as the relative density fluctuation remains small. In this case, the equivalence between the grand canonical and canonical ensembles is evident.

title: 7.3 Grand Canonical Ensemble
description: In physics, the canonical ensemble, which allows only energy exchange, does not cover all situations. Many systems also exchange particles with their surroundings, which calls for a more general framework: the grand canonical ensemble.

title: 7.8 The Meaning of the Maxwell Construction
description: It has been established that the pressure $P$ derived in the canonical ensemble coincides with that from the grand canonical ensemble if and only if $\partial P/\partial v \leq 0$. In this section, we demonstrate that when $\partial P/\partial v > 0$ for certain values of $v$ —a situation relevant only in theoretical contexts or non-equilibrium state— the pressure in the grand canonical ensemble is obtained from the that in the canonical ensemble via the Maxwell construction.
